assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's strontium clocks, brought fractional uncertainty to the 1e-18 level and underpin tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second. The idea is original and clean, the physics is transparent atomic physics, and the impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice trapping and demonstrated early Sr lattice clocks; Ye's group drove the record precision and comparisons. Two laureates is a natural, uncontroversial configuration. Other contributors (e.g. Lemonde, Ludlow, Lisdat, Hinkley) could be raised but the decisive credit is clear.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE, NIST) have confirmed 1e-18 performance; the field is mature and recognition is timely, with the redefinition process still in progress.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to pair this with Hall and Hansch frequency-comb work already recognised in 2005.
Ion-clock contributions (Wineland group already honoured in 2012) could blur the claim for optical lattice clocks specifically.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states opened an entirely new field of moire quantum matter with very broad and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery (with Cao, Fatemi et al., who are early-career coauthors and not on the credited list). The theory-plus-experiment configuration is attractive but leaves out Cao and others.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly and widely reproduced since 2018 by many groups and extended to other moire systems; the central discovery is robust though the mechanism of superconductivity is still debated.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism for superconductivity remains unresolved.
Credit for the experimental team beyond the senior author is a sensitive allocation issue.
Sixty-year-old versus young-researcher timing: the field is still young, so some may judge it premature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created a controllable platform for strong light-matter coupling with artificial atoms and the dominant architecture for superconducting quantum processors. It is original, conceptually clean in atomic-physics terms, and of very large technological and scientific consequence.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf proposed and demonstrated the architecture in 2004; I choose Schoelkopf, Wallraff and Girvin as the experimental and theoretical core, which unavoidably omits Blais and the Yale team members. Allocation is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many groups and enabling quantum-computing hardware; however the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is recent, and the committee may want some distance.
uncertainties: Overlap in community and subject with the 2025 prize.
Four credited names but a maximum of three laureates; Blais is omitted.
My view of atomic-physics analogies should not substitute for assessing the circuit-specific innovation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the time-reversal-invariant quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, and its experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells, established a major branch of topological quantum matter with wide influence on materials physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical prediction; Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted HgTe and Molenkamp's group observed the edge transport. Hasan's 3D realisation is also important. Any three-person set leaves out a significant contributor, notably Zhang (deceased) and Hasan.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmations across many materials and by many methods; the interpretation is stable. Part of the field was recognised in 2016 (Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz), so the conceptual novelty beyond that prize must be argued.
uncertainties: Whether 2D (HgTe) or 3D (Bi-based) realisations are better recognised and who should be credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for ion-trap quantum gates and Blatt's demonstrations of high-fidelity entangling operations and quantum simulation established the leading controlled quantum-computing platform in atomic physics.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the original theoretical proposal; Blatt delivered key experiments (Innsbruck). Wineland and Haroche were recognised in 2012 for single quantum systems, and others like Monroe and Wineland's NIST group contributed to the experimental gates and are not on this credited list.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced; commercial and academic platforms exist. Timeliness is reasonable, with the leading role of other platforms still debated.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with other candidates crediting Zoller and Cirac.
Experimental credit for Monroe and Wineland-group milestones is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised the Bose-Hubbard model, the Mott-superfluid transition and fermionic Hubbard physics with single-site resolution, giving a new quantum-simulation toolbox for many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Greiner, Hansch and Bloch observed the Mott transition; Esslinger's group realised fermionic Mott insulators; Jaksch, Zoller and Cirac proposed the Hubbard-model realisation. I choose the three principal experimentalists, leaving out the theoretical proposers; allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and widely replicated; the approach is firmly established and the results form a stable basis for further quantum simulation.
uncertainties: The theory-versus-experiment split of credit is unresolved.
The BEC prize in 2001 and the 2018 optical-tweezer prize give nearby recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and Berry's geometric phase revealed that phases of quantum states carry physical consequences and underlie a very wide range of phenomena, from molecular physics to topological matter. The concept is profound and original.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov (with Bohm, who died in 1992 and cannot be recognised) and Berry are clearly the decisive proposers of the two ideas; Pancharatnam and Longuet-Higgins have earlier precursors. The credited pair is clean, but the earlier Ehrenberg-Siday work and Bohm's role complicate the story.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally and theoretically firmly established for decades; recognition would be late rather than premature, which is a point of concern about whether a Nobel should still be awarded for such a long-established result.
uncertainties: Bohm is deceased and Ehrenberg-Siday precedence for the electron-phase effect exists.
Two distinct discoveries combined; they may not fit one coherent citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC completed the Standard Model and was a landmark of collective experimental physics, requiring decades of detector conception and construction.
assessment.attribution: The theory was recognised in 2013. The experimental recognition must reflect the conception and leadership of ATLAS and CMS; the three credited spokespersons/founders are plausible but the allocation among thousands of collaborators is inherently unfair and not resolvable from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: The boson is firmly confirmed with ongoing coupling measurements; recognition could be seen as overdue, though the collective nature of the discovery and the 2013 prize reduce the claim.
uncertainties: Inherent difficulty of recognising large collaborations within the three-person rule.
Whether other leaders (e.g. Gianotti, Incandela) have equal claim.
